Contents.Html:
[page[title]]

Move domain facts between handlers and application hosts without coupling business code to one transport.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • Typed in-process publish and subscribe through IEventHub.
  • HTTP handoff through the standard /Api/Eventing endpoint.
  • Azure Service Bus delivery behind the same event-provider shape.

Why the boundary matters

Domains raise meaningful events while deployment chooses whether delivery stays local, crosses HTTP or uses a message broker.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in ccoder.Eventing on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.Eventing" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddEventing();
builder.Services.AddEventingForType<OrderApproved>();

// Choose transport when the event crosses the process boundary:
builder.Services.AddHttpEventingWeb(/* options */);

Configure and run it

In-process delivery needs only the core Eventing package. HTTP and Azure Service Bus providers have separate packages and configuration; the application chooses transport while domain code continues to publish typed facts.

Consume the capability

Inject IEventHub, register handlers for the event type, and publish immutable domain facts. Use HTTP or Service Bus when deployment topology requires cross-process delivery rather than changing the business service.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/ccoder.Eventing.git
cd ccoder.Eventing
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
